purpose: Open-license pharmacology education sources to support foundational learning. This is not an approved clinical prescribing knowledge base.
ingestion_policy: Use only entries marked commercial_reuse_permitted for any extracted or adapted content in a commercial product, preserve attribution and license notices, track source versions, and have clinical summaries independently reviewed. Do not use any book as a current drug monograph or patient-specific medication authority.

sources.title: Nursing Pharmacology, 2nd edition
limits: The authors explicitly state this is not intended to be a drug reference book.
Designed for prelicensure nursing education, not dental prescribing decisions.
Any derived clinical card must be reviewed independently by a qualified clinician.

sources.title: Essentials of Pharmacology
sources.publisher: Medicine LibreTexts / University of Illinois Chicago
limits: Educational pharmacology text, not a current product label or patient-specific prescribing reference.
Check chapter-level license metadata for any third-party content before reuse.

Preclinical medical education reference, not a medication monograph or dental prescribing guideline.

sources.title: Public Health in Pharmacy Practice: A Casebook, 2nd edition
sources.source_verified_from: Official open textbook project and license statement
limits: Educational casebook, not a current drug monograph or dental prescribing guideline.
Check chapter-level attribution and exclude or separately clear any third-party materials before reuse.
Do not promote a teaching case into a patient-specific treatment recommendation without independent guideline review and qualified clinician approval.

sources.title: A Modified Delphi Study to Establish Essential Clinical Pharmacology Competencies
limits: Research about educational competencies, not a drug guideline or evidence for choosing a medicine.
Check article-level license text, figure/table notices, and any embedded third-party content before reuse.
Use to inform teaching objectives and assessment, not patient-specific treatment decisions.

sources.title: An innovative pharmacology curriculum for medical students: promoting higher order cognition, learner-centered coaching, and constructive feedback through a social pedagogy framework
limits: Educational-methods study, not a prescribing guideline or medicine safety database.
Check article-level license text, figure/table notices, and any embedded third-party content before reuse.
Use for designing learning workflows and feedback; do not infer patient-specific treatment recommendations.

sources.title: The use of generic versus brand names in (clinical) pharmacology education across Europe: a cross-sectional survey
limits: Research about naming and pharmacology education, not a clinical recommendation or medication equivalence checker.
Check article-level license text, figure/table notices, and any embedded third-party content before reuse.
Use to improve generic/brand teaching and retrieval; do not treat name similarity as proof of therapeutic interchangeability.

sources.title: PubMed Central Open Access Subset: Commercial Use Collection
sources.license_id: Article-level license required; commercial-use collection index
sources.source_verified_from: NCBI official PMC FTP and Open Access Subset documentation
limits: The collection index identifies articles available in a commercial-use collection; each article's license and files still need record-level validation.
Do not assume every article in PMC is reusable or available for commercial redistribution.
Use the official NCBI OA service and approved retrieval interfaces; do not scrape site pages.

sources.title: WHO Model List of Essential Medicines, 24th list (2025)
sources.license_id: WHO publication; verify record-specific terms before reuse
limits: Global policy/formulary reference, not a dental prescribing guideline or patient-specific recommendation.
Do not ingest full text into the commercial corpus until WHO's applicable reuse permission is confirmed.
Use as a linked source and policy context; verify jurisdiction and the local formulary before clinical application.

sources.title: Egypt: National Essential Medicine List 2025 (English)
authors: Ministry of Health and Population, Egypt
sources.license_id: National publication hosted by WHO; verify country/publisher reuse terms
limits: Use for Egyptian policy/formulary context only, not as a substitute for current local prescribing regulations or clinical guidelines.
Do not index full text for commercial use until reuse rights from the national publisher are confirmed.
Record country, publication year, and status; do not apply automatically to a US clinical workflow.

sources.title: CDC Dental Pain and Swelling Materials
authors: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.license_id: US government work generally public domain; check third-party items
limits: Use only within the patient population, scope, and clinical question addressed by the specific CDC guidance.
Confirm the current underlying fact sheet/guideline version and any third-party elements before reusing text.
Any derivative product clinical card must be reviewed and approved by a qualified dentist.

sources.title: American Association of Endodontists Clinical Guidelines and Position Statements
sources.license_id: Copyrighted professional guidance; reuse terms require confirmation
sources.source_verified_from: Official AAE guidelines and position statements index
limits: Guidelines vary by topic, publication date, and status; the page notes that some statements are under review.
Link-only until the exact document's reuse license or permission is confirmed.
Do not convert position statements into recommendations outside their clinical scope.

sources.title: Merck Manual Professional Edition
sources.license_id: Copyrighted; commercial reuse prohibited without written permission
limits: The official FAQ says users may share links but must not copy or commercially reuse text, images, audio, or video without written permission.
Never bulk-ingest or index full text into the commercial Dr. Mia corpus without explicit written permission.
Use source links for users to consult independently.

sources.title: Application of Emerging Teaching Models in Dental Education: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
limits: Educational-methods review, not a dental treatment or drug-prescribing guideline.
Check article-level license statement and any embedded third-party figure/table notices before reuse.
Useful for teaching architecture, not patient-specific medication decisions.

Review is foundational and must not replace a current product label or patient-specific clinician assessment.

authors: Indian Society of Periodontology working group

Indian professional guidance must not be automatically applied to US or Egypt practice.
Exact scope and recommendations require dental clinician review before any comparative teaching summary.
